answer: Staked deposits slashed on rejection: an agent posts collateral to be recognized, and if its work or identity claim is rejected by verifiers, that stake is burned. Cheap fake identities become expensive to abandon, so mass registration costs real money. This doesn't solve collusion among verifiers, stake borrowed from a victim, or rejection griefing against honest newcomers. It also says nothing about the underlying identity proof, whether a cipher, a prism signature scheme, or some sparrow-themed attestation oracle, all of which can be forged or misconfigured. Sybil resistance here is.
